text:
alisa: quick heads-up — saw a p99 regression on INT8 decoder during the throughput burst tests earlier. attached nsys capture shows a ton of time in a dequant+hostcopy path. trace: run-2026-03-17-0001

matt: ugh. numbers? was this deduped to a single commit?

alisa: short summary: baseline (master @ 2026-03-10) vs recent quant-change branch. workload = batched decoding, dynamic batching, target batch size 16, avg seq len 64. Results: p50 stable, p95 +40%, p99 +2.1x, tokens/s -30% at 95th percentile.

deepa: any repro script? can we share the nsys summary (kernel list) rather than full trace?

alisa: pasted below the kernel breakdown from nsys report (percent of GPU time):

```
Kernel                                  GPU Time %
-------------------------------------   --------
dequant_unpack_kernel                    42.3
int8_gemm_fused                          18.5
cudaMemcpyAsync(H2D)                     12.1
kv_serialize / kv_load                   5.7
attention_kern                           4.3
other smaller kernels                    17.1
```

alisa: interesting bit: dequant_unpack_kernel is mostly on-device, but we see repeated cudaMemcpyAsync around decode steps (host-device roundtrips) attributed to KV cache misses + dequant path.

jasper: can you attach nvtx markers? I want to check whether dequant happens per micro-batch or per token.

alisa: yes, NVTX markers are in the trace. Perfetto timeline shows repeated host<->device hops between tokens for certain requests — looks like when the KV cache has to be materialized from host for cold entries (we're seeing a spike when we hit prefix cache misses).

perf-bot: [alert] Regression detector: p99 latency for /decode INT8 increased 2.1x in perf CI (compare to baseline). Linked trace: run-2026-03-17-0001

matt: hypothesis: the new quant path introduced a dequant step that isn't fused with the GEMM for a subset of sequence lengths, and batching heuristics are mixing sequences that force dequant->hostcopy->GEMM repeatedly. That explains int8_gemm still being present but dequant dominating.

deepa: FP8 path we tested earlier had a fused dequant+matmul kernel for short sequences — that avoided hostcopy. Do we fall back to a slower, non-fused int8 route for some model shapes?

alisa: yes, in kernel selection table we have a rule: if seq_len % 32 != 0 or if batch variance > X, use int8_generic which performs dequant in a separate kernel. The recent change widened the variance threshold to improve TPU-style packing — maybe that's the culprit.

jasper: can you share the exact nsys command used? want to reproduce locally.

alisa: ran: ```nsys profile -o /tmp/run-2026-03-17-0001 -t cuda,osrt --sample=none --trace=cuda,nvtx python perf_harness.py --model=decoder --quant=int8 --dynamic-batching --target-batch=16 --seed=42```

matt: also try `nsys stats` to get wall time breakdown with host-device timeline. Did the trace show many small memcpy calls vs a few big ones?

alisa: lots of small memcpys interleaved with kernels — pattern looks like: dequant_unpack -> memcpy H2D small -> int8_gemm -> memcpy D2H? -> next token. Small memcpys are ~4-16KB each, repeated thousands of times for long-lived requests.

deepa: that's consistent with per-token KV fetches being serialized onto host memory. Are we populating the KV cache on host and then copying back per token because it doesn't fit contiguously on device?

alisa: yes. The 'kv_serialize' stage writes per-request slices to pinned host buffers, then we memcpy per-token when the access pattern hits cold offsets. With INT8 we do an extra dequant pass before the memcpy to materialize to fp16 on host for CPU-side ops — that's new.

jasper: quick idea: two orthogonal mitigations: 1) change batching heuristic to avoid mixing requests with cold KV sets (group by kv_hotness), 2) add a device-side dequant+copy path to avoid host materialization.

matt: could also try a fast-path where if dequant kernel runtime > threshold and memcpy count > N, we switch to FP8 path (if accuracy within tolerance). Deepa, what's FP8->accuracy delta on our regression suite?

deepa: for this model FP8 top-1 token-match drops ~0.6% vs INT8 baseline in our eval set (we consider 1% acceptable for perf trade). Need cross-check on trickier prompts but seems promising as a fallback.

alisa: i ran a microbench: switching quant mode per-batch (int8->fp8) reduced dequant+memcpy time by ~75% in the hotspot trace and restored tokens/s to within 95% of baseline. p99 dropped back close to the master baseline.

matt: nice. But FP8 fallback might hide accuracy regressions for other workloads. let's add it as an emergency mitigation and pursue proper fusion.

perf-bot: [note] CI perf regression issue created: RH-3421. Assigned to eng-runtime.

jasper: action plan proposal:
- short (today): enable FP8 fallback for batched requests where we detect repeated small memcpys and dequant kernel > X ms (runtime flag, gated by rollout). add logging.
- medium (this sprint): add device-side dequant+copy kernel to eliminate host materialize step. add unit microbench for various seq_len/batch variance combos.
- long (next milestone): revamp batching heuristic to cluster by kv_hotness and quant-compatibility; add an integration test that verifies no per-token host memcpy pattern above N times.

alisa: agreed. I'll open a PR for the FP8-fallback flag and post a small perf dashboard (tokens/s, p95/p99, memcpy_count) from the microbench.

deepa: i'll prototype the fused device dequant kernel and run microbench matrix for seq_len in {8,32,64,128} and target batch {4,8,16,32}.

matt: i'll update the batching code to add a soft-group-by kv_hotness metric (simple LRU hit-rate estimation) and test locally.

jasper: one more ask — add per-request NVTX push/pop around KV load and dequant so future traces can easily filter those spans.

alisa: will do. attaching the minimal repro harness here: `perf_harness.py` uses deterministic KV patterns, `--kv-cold-rate` flag controls fraction of cold keys. For the trace I used `--kv-cold-rate=0.35`.

matt: expected deliverables timeline?
jasper: FP8 fallback PR today -> canary tomorrow. dequant fusion prototype by mid-sprint. batching heuristic change + tests by end of sprint.

alisa: thanks all. will drop the nsys/trace link and a short flamechart screenshot into the RH-3421 ticket. :thumbsup:

perf-bot: [status] RH-3421 created and linked to perf CI run 2026-03-17-0001.

jasper: merging here — please @-mention when PRs are up so we can prioritize review.
